# Overview

This tutorial compares continuous cell states across eight CosMx non-small cell
lung cancer tissue sections from [He et al. (2022)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-022-01483-z).
We characterise tumour signatures, identify niches jointly across sections, and
compare correlations between cell state scores within those niches.

The analysis is adapted from the
[2025 spatial analysis workshop](https://github.com/bhuvad/CosMxSpatialAnalysisWorkshop/blob/49debcb8f7426825d4f2b0f193d7647199071f80/vignettes/Part_II_PhiSpace.Rmd)
by Jiadong Mao and Yifan Qin, preserved at tag `mig2025` (commit `49debcb8`).
It uses the workshop's 50% subsample: **350,228 segmented cells and 81 scores**
from five references. Four references cover immune, epithelial, endothelial
and mesenchymal lineages in lung fibrosis
([Natri et al., 2024](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-024-01702-0)); the fifth is
the lung cancer atlas of
[Salcher et al. (2022)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ccell.2022.10.008).

These are different inputs from the [four-reference CosMx case study](CosMx.html).
The supplied objects contain coordinates, metadata and precomputed PhiSpace
scores, with a placeholder expression assay. We retain the saved niche
memberships for the workshop example, recompute signatures and correlation
analyses, and compare a fresh joint clustering with the saved partition.
We cannot retrain the annotation from these objects.
For training and applying models, see [Stored PhiSpace models](StoredModels.html).

# Prepare the data

From a checkout of the PhiSpace repository, run
`Rscript --vanilla scripts/prepare-cosmx-multisample.R`. This downloads four
historical files from the pinned commit, verifies their SHA-256 checksums, and
converts them to `qs2`, checking that each restored object is identical.
The current workshop package is not needed. Set
`PHISPACE_COSMX_MULTISAMPLE_DATA` to the prepared folder when running this
article directly; its default is `Test/cosmx-multisample-inputs`.

```{r packages, message=FALSE}
library(PhiSpace)
library(SpatialExperiment)
library(ggplot2)
library(qs2)
library(vizOmics)

dat_dir <- Sys.getenv("PHISPACE_COSMX_MULTISAMPLE_DATA",
                      "Test/cosmx-multisample-inputs")
allTissues <- qs_read(file.path(dat_dir, "allTissues.qs2"), validate_checksum = TRUE)
historical <- qs_read(file.path(dat_dir, "historical-clusters.qs2"),
                      validate_checksum = TRUE)
out_dir <- file.path(dat_dir, "output")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
tissueNames <- c("Lung5_Rep1", "Lung5_Rep2", "Lung5_Rep3", "Lung6",
                 "Lung9_Rep1", "Lung9_Rep2", "Lung12", "Lung13")
stopifnot(identical(names(allTissues), tissueNames))
cell_ids <- unlist(lapply(allTissues, colnames), use.names = FALSE)
score_names <- colnames(reducedDim(allTissues[[1]], "PhiSpace"))
stopifnot(length(cell_ids) == 350228L, !anyDuplicated(cell_ids),
          length(score_names) == 81L,
          identical(cell_ids, names(historical$clusters)))
for (spe in allTissues) {
  score <- reducedDim(spe, "PhiSpace")
  stopifnot(identical(rownames(score), colnames(spe)),
            identical(colnames(score), score_names), all(is.finite(score)))
}
knitr::kable(data.frame(section = tissueNames,
                        cells = vapply(allTissues, ncol, integer(1))), row.names = FALSE)
```

Sections from the same lung are repeated measurements, rather than independent
patients. Spatial smoothing below is performed separately within each section,
so cells in different sections can never become neighbours.

## Pathology annotations

The `region` metadata contain the supplied pathology annotations. Missing
annotations are shown in grey. Colours have the same meaning in every panel;
each panel uses its own spatial extent.

```{r pathology-maps, fig.width=10, fig.height=14, message=FALSE, fig.cap="Supplied pathology annotations across the eight sections."}
region_names <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(allTissues, function(spe) as.character(spe$region)))))
region_cols <- setNames(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8, "Set2")[seq_along(region_names)], region_names)
plots <- lapply(tissueNames, function(s) {
  p <- VizSpatial(allTissues[[s]], colBy = "region", ptSize = 0.4,
             legend.symb.size = 2, fsize = 10) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = region_cols, limits = c(region_names, NA),
                         drop = FALSE, na.value = "grey80") +
    labs(title = s, colour = "Pathology") +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE,
                                 override.aes = list(size = 2)))
  # Draw keys for absent regions too, so every panel has the same legend.
  p$layers[[1]]$show.legend <- TRUE
  p
})
patchwork::wrap_plots(plots, ncol = 2, guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Tumour signatures

We fit partial least squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) separately in each
section, predicting pathology labels from the **unsmoothed** scores. As in the
workshop, the number of components equals the number of observed regions.
We rank states by their signed coefficient for `Tumour`. These coefficients
describe an association with the supplied label, rather than cell proportions.
Lung9_Rep2 has no labelled tumour region and is omitted from this comparison.

```{r tumour-signatures}
tumourNames <- setdiff(tissueNames, "Lung9_Rep2")
tumourSig <- regCoef_list <- setNames(vector("list", length(tumourNames)), tumourNames)
for (s in tumourNames) {
  query <- allTissues[[s]]
  query <- query[, !is.na(query$region)]
  fit <- rankFeatures(query, "region", method = "PLSDA",
                       ncomp = length(unique(query$region)))
  regCoef_list[[s]] <- fit$importance_scores
  tumourSig[[s]] <- selectFeat(fit$importance_scores, nfeat = 5,
                               absVal = FALSE)$orderedFeatMat[, "Tumour"]
}
tumour_table <- do.call(cbind, tumourSig)[1:10, , drop = FALSE]
```

The largest positive coefficient is at the top of each column. Scroll
horizontally to compare all seven sections.

```{r tumour-table, results='asis', echo=FALSE}
cat('<div class="table-responsive" style="overflow-x: auto;">',
    as.character(knitr::kable(tumour_table, format = "html", row.names = FALSE,
                              table.attr = 'style="white-space: nowrap;"')),
    '</div>')
```

Compare the signatures of the three Lung5 sections with those from other lungs.
A shared reference defines common score axes, but it does **not** guarantee
the absence of batch effects or make sections from one patient independent.

# Joint niche discovery

We smooth each section's scores over 15 neighbours with a Gaussian kernel,
concatenate sections in the declared order, and cluster the first 30 principal
components into nine niches. We retain the workshop's seed, Lloyd algorithm,
20 starts and 1,000-iteration limit. The scores are centred without scaling.

```{r joint-clustering, message=FALSE}
cluster_path <- file.path(out_dir, "joint-clusters.qs2")
if (!file.exists(cluster_path)) {
  smoothed <- lapply(allTissues, function(spe) {
    spatialSmoother(spe, smoothReducedDim = TRUE, kernel = "gaussian",
                     k = 15, include_self = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
  })
  mat2clust <- do.call(rbind, lapply(smoothed, function(spe) {
    reducedDim(spe, "PhiSpace_smoothed")
  }))
  multiClustRes <- clusterPhiSpace(
    mat2clust, k = 9, ncomp = 30, iter.max = 1000, nstart = 20,
    algorithm = "Lloyd", center = TRUE, scale = FALSE,
    seed = 83904, return_pca = FALSE
  )
  # Cluster numbers are arbitrary. Match labels by maximum overlap with the
  # saved workshop clustering, retaining the actual new memberships.
  overlap <- table(multiClustRes$clusters, historical$clusters[cell_ids])
  assignment <- clue::solve_LSAP(overlap, maximum = TRUE)
  label_map <- setNames(colnames(overlap)[as.integer(assignment)], rownames(overlap))
  joint_clusters <- setNames(unname(label_map[as.character(multiClustRes$clusters)]),
                             names(multiClustRes$clusters))
  # Adjusted Rand index compares memberships independently of cluster numbers.
  choose2 <- function(x) x * (x - 1) / 2
  a <- sum(choose2(rowSums(overlap)))
  b <- sum(choose2(colSums(overlap)))
  expected <- a * b / choose2(sum(overlap))
  historical_ari <- (sum(choose2(overlap)) - expected) / ((a + b) / 2 - expected)
  cluster_result <- list(
    clusters = joint_clusters, historical_ari = historical_ari,
    historical_agreement = mean(joint_clusters == as.character(historical$clusters[cell_ids])),
    parameters = multiClustRes$parameters,
    tot_withinss = multiClustRes$kmeans_result$tot.withinss
  )
  qs_save(cluster_result, cluster_path)
  rm(smoothed, mat2clust, multiClustRes)
  invisible(gc())
} else {
  cluster_result <- qs_read(cluster_path, validate_checksum = TRUE)
}
stopifnot(identical(names(cluster_result$clusters), cell_ids))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  comparison = c("Adjusted Rand index", "Agreement after matching labels"),
  value = c(cluster_result$historical_ari, cluster_result$historical_agreement)
), digits = 4)
```

The table compares the current computation with the saved workshop result.
The old PCA consumed random numbers before k-means; the current SVD does not.
This changes the random starts even with the same seed. A controlled replay
with the old random-number state recovers the saved partition exactly.
Matching labels alone does not change memberships. To preserve the workshop's
scientific example, the following maps, signatures and correlation analyses
use the **saved workshop memberships**, rather than transferring its
interpretations to a different partition. The fresh build still recomputes
joint clustering and reports its agreement above. A joint niche has the same
definition across sections, although its abundance and spatial arrangement can
differ.

```{r workshop-memberships}
analysis_clusters <- setNames(as.character(historical$clusters), names(historical$clusters))
for (s in tissueNames) {
  allTissues[[s]]$multiSampClust <- factor(
    analysis_clusters[colnames(allTissues[[s]])], levels = as.character(1:9)
  )
}
```

```{r niche-maps, fig.width=10, fig.height=14, message=FALSE, fig.cap="Saved workshop niche memberships, with the same colour for each niche across sections."}
niche_cols <- setNames(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(9, "Set1"), as.character(1:9))
plots <- lapply(tissueNames, function(s) {
  p <- VizSpatial(allTissues[[s]], colBy = "multiSampClust", ptSize = 0.4,
             legend.symb.size = 2, fsize = 10) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = niche_cols, limits = names(niche_cols), drop = FALSE) +
    labs(title = s, colour = "Joint niche")
  p$layers[[1]]$show.legend <- TRUE
  p
})
patchwork::wrap_plots(plots, ncol = 2, guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Characterise the niches

We summarise unsmoothed scores within each joint niche, selecting the five
states with the highest median. The boxplots use all cells in the niche.
To keep memory bounded, we calculate summaries before plotting rather than
reshaping all 28 million score entries into a long table. Whiskers extend to
the most extreme observations within 1.5 interquartile ranges; outliers are
omitted from the display.

```{r niche-signatures, fig.width=10, fig.height=14, fig.cap="The five states with the highest median unsmoothed score in each workshop niche."}
scores <- do.call(rbind, lapply(allTissues, function(spe) reducedDim(spe, "PhiSpace")))
joint <- analysis_clusters[rownames(scores)]
median_scores <- t(vapply(as.character(1:9), function(k) {
  apply(scores[joint == k, , drop = FALSE], 2, median)
}, numeric(ncol(scores))))
colnames(median_scores) <- score_names
rownames(median_scores) <- as.character(1:9)
box_data <- do.call(rbind, lapply(rownames(median_scores), function(k) {
  top <- names(sort(median_scores[k, ], decreasing = TRUE))[1:5]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(top, function(ct) {
    z <- scores[joint == k, ct]
    q <- quantile(z, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
    iqr <- q[3] - q[1]
    data.frame(niche = k, state = ct, median = q[2], lower = q[1], upper = q[3],
               ymin = min(z[z >= q[1] - 1.5 * iqr]),
               ymax = max(z[z <= q[3] + 1.5 * iqr]))
  }))
}))
box_data$key <- factor(paste(box_data$niche, box_data$state),
                       levels = paste(box_data$niche, box_data$state)[order(box_data$niche, box_data$median)])
ggplot(box_data, aes(x = key, fill = median, ymin = ymin, lower = lower,
                     middle = median, upper = upper, ymax = ymax)) +
  geom_boxplot(stat = "identity") + coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ niche, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) sub("^[0-9]+ ", "", x)) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "white", high = "red") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) + labs(x = NULL, y = "PhiSpace score", fill = "Median")
```

We also compare the joint niches with the supplied pathology labels. This
provides a check on the interpretation of each niche, rather than relying on
its numeric label. The old chapter called niches 1, 3 and 6 cancer niches,
but that grouping does not agree with the supplied pathology annotations.

```{r niche-pathology}
pathology_table <- table(
  niche = joint,
  pathology = unlist(lapply(allTissues, function(spe) as.character(spe$region)), use.names = FALSE)
)
knitr::kable(data.frame(niche = rownames(pathology_table),
                        as.data.frame.matrix(round(prop.table(pathology_table, 1), 3)),
                        check.names = FALSE),
              row.names = FALSE)
```

# Cell state co-presence

Here, **co-presence** means Pearson correlation between unsmoothed PhiSpace
scores across cells within a niche and section. It can reflect shared
transcriptional programmes, mixtures of identities or measurement effects.
It does not establish physical contact, communication or a causal interaction
between cell types. For each section–niche combination with at least 50 cells,
we calculate an 81 by 81 correlation matrix and vectorise its lower triangle.

```{r co-presence}
minNicheCells <- 50L
corMat_list <- list()
cor_metadata <- list()
for (s in tissueNames) {
  query <- allTissues[[s]]
  sc <- reducedDim(query, "PhiSpace")
  for (k in unique(as.character(query$multiSampClust))) {
    keep <- query$multiSampClust == k
    if (sum(keep) < minNicheCells) next
    key <- paste(k, s, sep = "_")
    corMat_list[[key]] <- cor(sc[keep, , drop = FALSE])
    cor_metadata[[key]] <- data.frame(niche = k, sample = s, cells = sum(keep))
  }
}
cor_metadata <- do.call(rbind, cor_metadata)
pair_names <- outer(score_names, score_names, function(x, y) paste0(x, "<->", y))
corMatVec <- t(vapply(corMat_list, function(x) x[lower.tri(x)],
                      numeric(choose(length(score_names), 2))))
colnames(corMatVec) <- pair_names[lower.tri(pair_names)]
stopifnot(all(is.finite(corMatVec)), identical(rownames(corMatVec), rownames(cor_metadata)))
dim(corMatVec)
```

As an example, we show one tumour-associated niche in Lung5_Rep1, selecting
25 score columns with the highest variance across its correlation matrix.
This is a display selection; all 3,240 pairs enter the subsequent analyses.

```{r example-correlation, fig.width=9, fig.height=9}
example_cor <- corMat_list[["1_Lung5_Rep1"]]
selected <- names(sort(apply(example_cor, 2, var), decreasing = TRUE))[1:25]
plotCorrelation(example_cor[selected, selected], seriation_method = "PCA")
```

## Compare correlation patterns by PCA

Each point below represents a section–niche correlation matrix. We retain
five PCs and display the first two. Similar scores indicate similar
correlation patterns, which need not imply similar mean state scores.

```{r correlation-pca}
set.seed(12361)
pca_res <- getPC(corMatVec, ncomp = 5)
pca_plot <- data.frame(pca_res$scores, cor_metadata)
ggplot(pca_plot, aes(comp1, comp2, colour = niche, label = sample)) +
  geom_text(size = 2.8, check_overlap = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = niche_cols) + theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "PC1", y = "PC2", colour = "Joint niche")
plotLoadings(pca_res$loadings, "comp1", showNeg = FALSE, absVal = TRUE, nfeat = 10)
plotLoadings(pca_res$loadings, "comp2", showNeg = FALSE, absVal = TRUE, nfeat = 10)
```

## Exploratory discriminant analysis

We use distance-weighted discrimination (DWD) to contrast niches in which
more than half the **pathology-labelled cells** are labelled `Tumour` with
the remaining niches. This explicit, illustrative threshold replaces the
old chapter's inconsistent hard-coded niche numbers. Cells without pathology
labels do not enter the denominator. DWD produces a fitted score and a weight
for each pair of cell states.

```{r dwd}
tumour_fraction <- prop.table(pathology_table, 1)[, "Tumour"]
tumour_niches <- names(tumour_fraction)[tumour_fraction > 0.5]
tumour_niches
nicheBinary <- ifelse(cor_metadata$niche %in% tumour_niches, 1, -1)
dwd_res <- rankFeatures(corMatVec, response = nicheBinary,
                        method = "DWD", seed = 12361)
dwd_plot <- data.frame(dwd_res$scores,
                       group = ifelse(nicheBinary == 1, "Tumour-majority niches", "Other niches"))
ggplot(dwd_plot, aes(DWD_score, fill = group)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) + theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Fitted DWD score", fill = NULL)
plotLoadings(dwd_res$importance_scores, "DWD_weight", nfeat = 20)
```

These are fitted, exploratory contrasts. The display does not measure
prediction on independent patients, and the internal cross-validation used
to choose regularisation does not account for repeated sections from one
lung. Clinical or predictive claims would require validation that holds out
entire patients.

```{r save-validation, include=FALSE}
metrics <- list(
  n_sections = length(allTissues), n_cells = length(cell_ids), n_states = length(score_names),
  cells_sha256 = digest::digest(cell_ids, algo = "sha256"),
  states_sha256 = digest::digest(score_names, algo = "sha256"),
  tumour_table_sha256 = digest::digest(tumour_table, algo = "sha256"),
  dwd_tumour_niches = paste(tumour_niches, collapse = ","),
  historical_ari = cluster_result$historical_ari,
  historical_agreement = cluster_result$historical_agreement,
  recomputed_tot_withinss = cluster_result$tot_withinss,
  n_cor_matrices = nrow(corMatVec), n_cor_pairs = ncol(corMatVec),
  cor_mean = mean(corMatVec), cor_sd = sd(as.vector(corMatVec)),
  cor_abs_sum = sum(abs(corMatVec)),
  pca_score_ss = sum(pca_res$scores^2),
  dwd_score_mean = mean(dwd_res$scores[, "DWD_score"]),
  dwd_score_sd = sd(dwd_res$scores[, "DWD_score"]),
  dwd_weight_abs_sum = sum(abs(dwd_res$importance_scores))
)
for (s in tissueNames) metrics[[paste0(s, "_n_cells")]] <- ncol(allTissues[[s]])
for (k in as.character(1:9)) {
  metrics[[paste0("niche_", k, "_size")]] <- sum(joint == k)
  metrics[[paste0("niche_", k, "_tumour_fraction")]] <- prop.table(pathology_table, 1)[k, "Tumour"]
}
qs_save(metrics, file.path(out_dir, "CosMxMultiSample-summary.qs2"))
```

# Provenance and further reading

The tutorial retains the workshop's supplied scores and subsampling, while
updating compatibility with current PhiSpace APIs. Source and input hashes,
the fresh/cached build procedure and numerical comparisons are recorded in
the repository's `scripts/cosmx-multisample-validation.md`. No expression
normalisation or reference fitting is performed by this tutorial.

For the scientific method and broader spatial analyses, see
[Mao, Choi and Lê Cao (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.crmeth.2026.101483).
The original workshop is distributed under GPL-3.0; its authorship and source
are retained above.
